Unrest, Regions, History and Glory
Four mechanics that give the game its tension: what clogs you, what produces, what you put into History, and what scores big.
Unrest
They have no useful effect and dilute your deck. If the common pile runs out, it is a Collapse. Three ways to get rid of them:
Play it as an Action
: spend an Action token, then pay 3
, or 1
, or discard 2 cards. It goes back to the pile.
The Pacify order
: it takes your whole turn, but you return all the Unrest in your hand without paying anything.
A card effect
that says "Return an Unrest card": you then ignore the Unrest text, so no cost.
Recovering an Unrest means taking it from the common pile. Taking the last one triggers the Collapse.
Regions and cards in play
A permanent card stays in your play area until an effect removes it.
a Region: it goes to your discard pile.
a Region: it returns to your hand. Only Regions can be Abandoned or Recalled.

In both cases, resources placed on it return to your reserve, and cards Reserved under it follow the Region. An Exhaust token placed on it doesn't return to your State card before the end of the turn.
Reserve

: slide a card from your hand, face up, under the card in play that carries this keyword. A Reserved card is no longer in play: you can't play it, discard it or use its abilities. It still counts for scoring. It is a good way to slim down your deck.
History

Putting a card into your History means sliding it under your Power card. It leaves play for good, but its points still count. You may look at your own History, not other players'. Many strong cards are single-use and go into History after being played.

The Fame deck and King of Kings
The King of Kings card always stays at the very bottom of the Fame deck. While face-down cards remain, Looking at, gaining or Drawing a Fame card only concerns those.
A card put back into this deck goes on top, without shuffling.
When King of Kings is the only card left, any effect that makes you gain or Draw a Fame card makes you
resolve King of Kings
instead. The first time in the game, it is flipped to side B.
Each player can only resolve it once per game, whichever side.
When the card ends up flipped face down, the Countdown is triggered.

Does a card in your History count for scoring?
It is no longer in play, but its victory points count.

Four settings to adjust the game, and a solo learning mode.
Training mode (alone, no opponent)
Ideal for a first try or to discover a nation.
Set up as for 2 players.
Exile the top 15 cards of the Main deck.
Put 12 Progress tokens near the Market: it is your hourglass.
Play your turns normally.
At Cleanup, the Progress placed on the Market comes from this hourglass. Then you may Exile a Market card, to simulate an opponent helping themselves.
Resolve your Solstice effects after each turn.
The game lasts 12 turns, or stops if an effect triggers the end.
Rulebook benchmarks: 50 points, you master the basics; 90 points is a feat.
Pacifist variant
During setup, set aside the common cards marked with the Attack icon. Once the Market is laid out, shuffle them into the Main deck. Attacks thus arrive later.
Precious cards variant
At Cleanup, you can no longer Discard cards from your hand. Managing Unrest becomes much tighter.
Quick game variant
About 15 minutes less per player.
Once the Market is set up, Exile the top 10 cards of the Main deck.
Each player discards the top 2 cards of their Nation deck: they are therefore part of their deck from the first shuffle.
When you add your Accession to your discard pile, choose one of your Development cards and remove it from the game.
At the Countdown, finish the current round and its Solstice, with no extra round.
Quick setup variant

For experienced players: shuffle all the Market cards together instead of sorting them, form the decks with the right number of cards and flip one card from each. Some nations will struggle to find the categories they need.

When the Main deck is empty

Playing solo against the Bot
The Bot is an automated opponent. It doesn't read the text of its cards: the table on its State card tells it what to do.
The Play solo tab applies everything below for you: you just follow its instructions.
Set up your nation and the Market as for 2 players.
Place the slot markers 1 to 5 under the five Market cards (see difficulty levels).
Choose the Bot's nation. Its starting Unrest cards join the common pile. Its Power card is only used to hold its History.
Build its
Dynasty deck
: the Developments sorted by value, strongest on top; on top of them the Accession face up; on top of that the shuffled Nation cards, face down.
Shuffle its starting cards and place one face down under each marker. The rest forms the Bot deck.
Place its State card on the Barbarian side. The Bot uses neither Action nor Exhaust tokens.
A round
You play your turn normally, then the Bot plays its turn, then you resolve your Solstice effects. The Bot ignores the Solstice.
The Bot's turn
Roll the die and place it on the card in the matching slot: it won't be resolved this turn. If no slot matches, all cards are resolved.
Resolve the other cards in ascending slot order. For each: flip it, look in the table for the
first line from the top
matching its name, type or category, and apply it as much as possible. Bold text concerns you, the rest concerns the Bot.
If nothing in the line can be resolved, move to the next matching line. As soon as part of the effect resolves, that card is done: one effect per card.
The card then goes to the Bot's discard pile, unless stated otherwise. The first line always concerns Unrest: usually, back to the pile.
Its Cleanup
Add 1 Progress on the Market card above the unresolved card. Nothing if the die showed 6. Against the Carthaginians, it is 2 Materials instead.
Slide the unresolved card to slot 1, face down, then fill the other slots from the Bot deck.
Deck empty when filling: the top card of the Dynasty deck goes to its discard pile, which is shuffled to rebuild the deck. When it is the Accession, flip its State card and use the new table.
How it chooses
Acquire or Innovate
: the Market card worth the most points; if tied, the one carrying the most tokens; then the lowest slot number. Each Progress placed on a card makes it worth 1 more point in its eyes.
Cards it gains go
on top of its deck
: the card first, the Unrest on top.
If it must Innovate with no valid card, it takes the top card of the relevant deck; if that is impossible, it gains 2 Progress.
: the lowest slot with no token.
Abandon / Recall
: its most recently played Region (to its discard pile, or on top of its deck).
It only shuffles its discard pile during its Cleanup.

It ignores your effects that would make it Discard or Return an Unrest. Any effect of its that gives you an Unrest, steals from you, makes you discard, Abandon or Recall counts as an Attack: your protections work.
For the Bot, a variable-points card is worth 5, and a conditional card is worth its maximum.
End of the game
Same triggers as in multiplayer, plus two: the Dynasty deck is exhausted, or the Bot gains King of Kings.
If the game ends in a Collapse, you lose.

At the Countdown, the Bot scores 1 point per Progress, 1 point per group of 10 Materials and Population combined, and its card points (hand, play, deck, discard, History; not the Dynasty deck or its Power card). You need strictly more points than it.
